v01-alameda.name: Alameda
tags: Michelin one star (awarded March 2026 — Faro's first ever)
v01-alameda.why: Michelin one star (awarded March 2026 — Faro's first ever). To order: the tasting menu — Origami (12 courses) or Umami (8 courses) — the kitchen reads the Ria, oyster with eucalyptus ponzu and lime, octopus from Olhão, smoked eel. Chef Rui Sequeira, ex-Ocean (Hans Neuner) and direct alumnus of the Vila Vita kitchen. The star reads as a line drawn under three decades of Algarve being only resort cooking. Thu–Mon dinner, Sunday lunch slots.
v01-alameda.address: Rua da Polícia da Segurança Pública 10, 8000 Faro
v01-alameda._lane: The starred tables — Faro's first star and the two-star kitchens of the coast

v16-vila-joya.name: Vila Joya
tags: Michelin two stars — held since 1999, the longest-running ★★ on the Algarve coast
v16-vila-joya.why: Michelin two stars — held since 1999, the longest-running ★★ on the Algarve coast. To order: the daily-changing tasting; no dish appears twice across the year. Austrian chef Dieter Koschina, in the Algarve since 1991; first star 1995, second 1999 — the first ★★ in Portugal. 30 seats. Cliffside Atlantic terrace.
v16-vila-joya.address: Estrada da Galé, Praia da Galé, 8201-902 Albufeira
v16-vila-joya._lane: The starred tables — Faro's first star and the two-star kitchens of the coast

v17-ocean-restaurant.name: Ocean Restaurant
tags: Michelin two stars since 2011; Best Service Award 2026
v17-ocean-restaurant.why: Michelin two stars since 2011; Best Service Award 2026. To order: the discovery menu — Atlantic fish read through Portugal's Age of Discovery routes. Chef Hans Neuner (Portugal's Chef of the Year 2009 and 2012). Rui Sequeira of Alameda passed through this kitchen — the lineage is direct.
v17-ocean-restaurant._lane: The starred tables — Faro's first star and the two-star kitchens of the coast

v03-estamin-ilha-deserta.name: Estaminé — Ilha Deserta
tags: The cult lunch of southern Portugal — solar-powered restaurant on an uninhabited barrier island
v03-estamin-ilha-deserta.why: The cult lunch of southern Portugal — solar-powered restaurant on an uninhabited barrier island. To order: whatever the Ria gave that morning — oysters, grilled sea bream, conquilhas, arroz de lingueirão; the tuna and octopus estupetas. Animaris ferry from the marina (~30 min through the lagoon, return ~€10). Rebuilt August 2021 after a March fire. Photovoltaic plant covers all energy; seawater desalination for drinking water. First boat out, last boat back.
v03-estamin-ilha-deserta.address: Ilha da Barreta — Animaris boat from Cais das Portas do Mar, Faro marina
v03-estamin-ilha-deserta._lane: Tables with a story — an island lunch, a chef who gave back his star, a cellar under the walls

v02-checkin-by-leonel-pereira.name: CHECKin by Leonel Pereira
v02-checkin-by-leonel-pereira.why: Michelin Bib Gourmand (2025/2026). To order: the seasonal menu — Check-in / Cozinhados no Tacho / Momentos Especiais / Check-out; ask the sommelier for niche Portuguese producers. Leonel Pereira held a star at São Gabriel (Almancil), gave it up to open a more democratic concept inside the walls. 26 seats indoors + 30-seat terrace. Wine list among the most curious in the city.
v02-checkin-by-leonel-pereira._lane: Tables with a story — an island lunch, a chef who gave back his star, a cellar under the walls

v05-faz-gostos.name: Faz Gostos
tags: Michelin Plate — local gastronomic reference inside the walls
v05-faz-gostos.why: Michelin Plate — local gastronomic reference inside the walls. To order: arroz de marisco (≈ €40 for two), cataplana, the day's fish. Established 2009. Two halls (up to 150 covers — unusually large for Michelin-listed but the consistency holds). 18th-c. underground wine cellar. Modern Algarve cooking that opens the Cidade Velha to serious eaters.
v05-faz-gostos._lane: Tables with a story — an island lunch, a chef who gave back his star, a cellar under the walls
